output.one_liner: Shopify is an e-commerce platform that lets merchants build and manage online stores with products, orders, customers, and inventory management.

auth.notes: Public and custom apps use OAuth2. Access tokens are sent as X-Shopify-Access-Token header. Composio catalog also lists S2S_OAuth2 for server-to-server authentication.

evidence.snippet: Public and custom apps created in the Dev Dashboard generate tokens using OAuth
Every GraphQL Admin API request carries an access token in the X-Shopify-Access-Token header.

access.notes: Developers can create free dev stores and obtain API credentials immediately without restriction. Public app distribution via App Store requires vendor review, but development and testing is unrestricted.

evidence.snippet: Sign in to your Shopify admin. If you don't have a store, start one at shopify.com.
Publish your app in the Shopify App Store and any merchant can install it once it passes review.

api_surface.rate_limit_note: Shopify enforces rate limits covering input array size, pagination depth, and API-specific limits.

evidence.snippet: GraphQL Admin API reads and writes products, customers, orders, inventory, and the rest of the data behind the Shopify admin.
The REST Admin API is a legacy API as of October 1, 2024.
You can use webhook subscriptions to receive notifications about particular events in a shop.
Shopify MCP is a remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets merchants build and run a Shopify store through the AI agent of their choice.

buildability.rationale: Self-serve free credentials, documented REST and GraphQL APIs with broad resource coverage, and webhook support enable immediate toolkit development without barriers.

overview_evidence.snippet: Reference documentation for Shopify's APIs, libraries, and developer tools, plus the concepts that apply across all of them.
This toolkit is GraphQL-first for new Admin API automations while retaining legacy REST compatibility actions for older workflows.
